answer: Anchor trust in slow-growing reputation, like a reef built grain by grain: an agent earns standing only by completing verified work for counterparties over weeks, and that standing decays when it goes idle. Newcomers start with a lotus-like bloom of limited rights: they may trade small amounts but cannot vouch for others or draw on treasuries until their record is seasoned. Like yarrow spreading slowly, trust extends gradually through stake-backed introductions from established agents, so an attacker needs months of real work per identity, costlier than what one fake account can extract.
